title: Percentages
subject: Mathematics

English.simple_explanation: A percentage says how many parts you have out of every hundred, which lets you compare things that started from different totals.
English.detailed_explanation:
Per cent means per hundred. Writing 45% is the same as writing the fraction 45/100, or the decimal 0.45. To turn any score into a percentage, divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100.

The reason this matters is comparison. Eighteen marks out of twenty and twenty-seven out of thirty are hard to rank by eye, because the totals differ. Convert them and the question answers itself: 18/20 is 90% and 27/30 is 90%, so the two performances are identical even though neither the marks nor the totals match.

A percentage is always a percentage of something, and forgetting what that something is causes most of the mistakes. A 50% increase followed by a 50% decrease does not return you to where you began, because the second 50% is taken from a larger number than the first was added to.

common_misconceptions: A percentage is just another word for the number of marks you scored.
Adding 50% and then taking away 50% brings you back to the number you started with.
You can add two percentages together even when they are percentages of different totals.

observe_around_you.invitation: Find two of your own marked papers where the totals are different — say one out of 20 and one out of 50.
observe_around_you.what_to_do: Write down both scores. Decide which one you think was your better performance. Then convert both to percentages: divide the marks by the total and multiply by 100.
observe_around_you.what_to_notice: Did the percentages agree with your guess? Look especially at whether the paper with the higher mark was really the better result.
observe_around_you.concept_link: Raw marks cannot be compared across different totals, which is exactly the job a percentage does. It puts both scores on the same scale of a hundred so the comparison becomes fair.
needs: two of your own marked papers with different totals

think_question: A shop raises a price by 20%, then later reduces it by 20%. Is the final price the same as the original? Explain your reasoning before calculating.

reasoning_guide.correct_feedback: Good reasoning: you noticed the second percentage is taken from a different, larger amount.
reasoning_guide.partial_feedback: You have started well. Say what number each percentage is calculated from, and whether those two numbers are the same.
reasoning_guide.misconception_feedback: The price does not return to where it began. The 20% rise is taken from the original price, but the 20% fall is taken from the raised price, which is larger.

challenge.question: A student scored 36 out of 45 in a test. What is the score as a percentage?
challenge.hint: Divide the marks by the total, then multiply by 100.
progressive_hints: Divide the marks by the total, then multiply by 100.

quiz_questions.question: What does 65% mean?
quiz_questions.explanation: Per cent means per hundred, so 65% is 65 out of every 100.
quiz_questions.hint: Break the word apart: per and cent.
progressive_hints: Break the word apart: per and cent.
Cent means hundred, as in a century.

quiz_questions.question: Which is the better score: 21 out of 25, or 32 out of 40?
quiz_questions.explanation: 21/25 is 84% and 32/40 is 80%, so 21 out of 25 is the stronger result even though it is fewer marks.
quiz_questions.hint: Convert both to percentages before comparing.
progressive_hints: Convert both to percentages before comparing.

quiz_questions.question: A shirt costs 800 rupees and is reduced by 25%. What is the new price?
quiz_questions.hint: Work out the discount first, then subtract it.
progressive_hints: Work out the discount first, then subtract it.
25% is one quarter, and a quarter of 800 is 200.

sources: Standard Class 8-10 mathematics: percentage as parts per hundred, conversion between fraction, decimal and percentage, and percentage change. Academic review is still needed.
